sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Ewing Township different?
sections.html:
Ewing requires every home sold in the township to pass a housing inspection first, so the main variable in a fast sale is how quickly the property can pass that check. The rest of the process is the usual New Jersey deed, transfer fee and tax filings.

Ewing sits in Mercer County on the Delaware River, directly north and west of Trenton. It covers about 15.6 square miles, and the 2020 Census counted 37,264 residents, the highest count in the township's history. The Census Bureau estimated 39,030 people in July 2025, a rise of 4.5 percent from the 2020 base. The 2020 density was about 2,450 people per square mile of land.

sections.h2: How did Ewing Township grow into the community it is today?
sections.html:
Ewing became a township on February 22, 1834, cut from Trenton Township and named in honor of Charles Ewing, a former chief justice of the New Jersey Supreme Court. It joined the new Mercer County in 1838. Before that the land was mostly farms and small hamlets: Carleton is now Ewing, Cross Keys is Ewingville, and Birmingham is West Trenton.

The township grew as a suburb of Trenton through the 20th century. Its population rose from 6,942 in 1930 to 26,628 by 1960 and has stayed between about 32,800 and 37,300 since 1970. Blocks near the Trenton line are distinctly urban, while most of the township is residential subdivisions.

Neighborhood names show up in listings and appraisals, so use the local one. Examples include Ewingville, West Trenton, Prospect Heights, Fernwood, Hillwood Lakes, Parkway Village, Scudders Falls and Wilburtha. Many were built in separate phases, and house styles change noticeably from one to the next.

sections.html:
Ewing prices sit below the national median value, and rental households make up a third of the township. The table lists the 2020 to 2024 Census QuickFacts estimates against national figures.

sections.h2: Which employers and institutions anchor the Ewing market?
sections.html:
Ewing hosts several large public employers, which keeps demand for housing steady among staff who want a short commute. The Katzenbach School for the Deaf and the Trenton-Mercer Airport are also located in the township.

Church and Dwight moved its corporate headquarters from Princeton to Ewing in 2013. The township also absorbed a major loss: the Naval Air Warfare Center Trenton on Parkway Avenue operated from 1953 until 1997 and closed under the 1993 base closure recommendations, ending nearly 700 civilian positions. The Jones Farm, the last working farm in Ewing, shut at the end of 2022.

  • Education and public safety: The College of New Jersey and State Police headquarters.
  • State agencies: the Department of Transportation headquarters and Trenton Psychiatric Hospital.
  • Private employers: Church and Dwight, plus the Community Blood Council of New Jersey.

sections.h2: Which roads and rail lines serve Ewing homes?
sections.html:
Four major roads cross the township, and the West Trenton rail terminal anchors the commuter side. Interstate 295 crosses the northwest corner, Route 29 follows the Delaware River as the Delaware River Scenic Byway, U.S. Route 206 skirts the southeast, and Route 31 (Pennington Road) runs north to Pennington and Flemington.

West Trenton station is the terminus of SEPTA's West Trenton Line, which mainly carries riders to Philadelphia. NJ Transit buses 601, 607, 608, 609 and 624 connect the township with Trenton. Trenton-Mercer Airport, open since 1929 and served by Frontier Airlines, is also inside Ewing's borders.

The Delaware and Raritan Canal passes near the river, and the strip of land along it is part of the Delaware and Raritan Canal State Park. Homes along River Road and Route 29 sit near the water, so check flood-zone status with the township before quoting a price to a buyer who asks.

sections.h2: How do schools and weather affect an Ewing house?
sections.html:
Ewing Public Schools run prekindergarten through twelfth grade in one district, with five schools: Antheil, Lore and Parkway elementary schools, Fisher Middle School and Ewing High School. Enrollment was 3,444 students in the 2020 to 2021 school year. The district is also known for the 1946 case Everson v. Board of Education, a U.S. Supreme Court decision on bus transport for parochial school students.

The climate is hot-summer humid continental. Based on 1991 to 2020 normals, the township averages 48.2 inches of precipitation a year and about 8 inches of snow in each of January and February.

That much rain is why the housing inspector looks at grading and drainage, roofs, gutters and foundation walls. Fixing a downspout that empties against the foundation costs little and removes an easy objection before the inspection.

sections.h2: What does Ewing's resale inspection check?
sections.html:
Every dwelling or commercial building offered for resale must be inspected and approved by the Ewing Division of Housing, and the residential fee on the township's 2025 form is $125. The inspector works from the International Property Maintenance Code and township ordinances. Requests can be made through the township's SDL portal, which needs an account, or through the Construction Office at 1666 Pennington Road, 609-883-2900, extension 7676.

The township's printed checklist is not limited to these items, but they come up often:

  • Smoke alarms on every level, using ten-year sealed lithium battery single-station units, and carbon monoxide alarms within 10 feet of sleeping areas.
  • A portable fire extinguisher rated at least 2A-10B:C within 10 feet of the kitchen, mounted no higher than 5 feet, and tagged or receipted within the last 12 months.
  • Ground-fault outlets in kitchens, baths and outdoors, and at least two receptacles per bedroom.
  • Sound handrails, stairs, roofs, windows with screens, and working heating equipment.
  • No double-keyed deadbolts, which the form calls illegal.
  • All open permits closed out, and a well water certificate where a well serves the house.

Some repairs may need Uniform Construction Code permits, so call the office before hiring a contractor.

sections.h2: What if the Ewing house is a rental?
sections.html:
Rental houses carry extra paperwork in Ewing, and the registration status should be settled before a sale. Under township ordinance 10-07, residential rentals must be registered every year regardless of tenant changes, with the registration and rental fire prevention forms due January 31. Landlords also need a property maintenance inspection whenever a tenant changes.

If you sell a rental, give the buyer the registration record, the latest fire prevention form and any open violation notices. A buyer who wants to occupy the house will need the unit vacated on a schedule written into the contract.

sections.h2: What are the closing costs and recording steps in Ewing?
sections.html:
The seller pays the state Realty Transfer Fee, and the deed is recorded with the Mercer County Clerk in Trenton, whose office has kept property records since 1838. For total consideration of $350,000 or less, the state schedule runs $2.00 per $500 up to $150,000, $3.35 per $500 from $150,000 to $200,000 and $3.90 per $500 from $200,000 to $350,000. Ask the closing attorney for the final figure.

The county charges $43 for the first page of a regular deed and $10 for each additional page. Realty transfer fees must be paid by cash, cashier's check, money order, attorney trust account or business escrow account, and amounts over $10,000 by certified or bank check. Mercer's land records page also notes that the transfer fee on sales of $1 million and above, often called the mansion tax, changed on July 10, 2025 so that the seller pays it.

New Jersey residents sign a GIT/REP-3 at closing. A nonresident owner owes an estimated payment of at least 2 percent of the price unless an exemption applies.

faqs.q: Is an inspection required to sell a house in Ewing?
faqs.a: Yes. The Division of Housing must inspect and approve every dwelling offered for resale in the township. The residential fee on the 2025 form is $125, and requests go through the SDL portal or the Construction Office at 609-883-2900, extension 7676.

faqs.q: What alarms does a Ewing resale inspection require?
faqs.a: The township asks for smoke alarms on every level, using ten-year sealed lithium battery single-station units, and carbon monoxide alarms within 10 feet of sleeping areas. It also asks for a labeled fire extinguisher near the kitchen that is tagged or receipted within 12 months.

faqs.q: How much does the Mercer County Clerk charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: A regular deed costs $43 for the first page and $10 for each added page. The state transfer fee is paid separately at recording and is set by the sale price. The county clerk accepts cash, cashier's check, money order, attorney trust account or business escrow account for that fee.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental before selling it in Ewing?
faqs.a: Registration is a yearly requirement under ordinance 10-07, with forms due January 31, so it should already be on file. Landlords also need a property maintenance inspection on each tenant change. Bring the paperwork to the sale so the buyer sees a clean record.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Ewing house with open permits?
faqs.a: Open permits must be closed out before the resale inspection can be passed, according to the township's inspection list. Call the Construction Office to learn what final inspections are outstanding. Some repairs also need new Uniform Construction Code permits before work begins.
